title: Binding Multi-bit Flip-flop Cells through Design and Technology Co-optimization
problem: Multi-bit flip-flop cells are constrained by inflexibility in optimizing D/Q-pin wiring due to large cell size and inability to selectively resize internal flip-flops for timing control. These limitations prevent full optimization despite MBFF's dynamic power benefits.
motivation: MBFFs reduce dynamic power consumption, but fundamental design constraints prevent their full exploitation in physical design optimization.
method: Design-technology co-optimization applies MBFF rebinding in two stages: (1) post-placement explores diverse MBFF layouts with different D/Q-pin locations and rebinds instances to minimize wirelength, (2) post-route explores non-rectangular L- and T-shaped layouts enabling selective control of internal flip-flop driving strength, rebinding negative-slack instances to optimize timing while minimizing power overhead.
key_novelty: Using DTCO-driven rebinding with non-rectangular MBFF cell layouts to simultaneously address wirelength and timing constraints.
contributions: Post-placement MBFF rebinding algorithm exploring diverse D/Q-pin configurations
Non-rectangular MBFF cell layouts (L- and T-shapes) enabling selective driving strength control
Post-route timing optimization strategy with minimal power penalty
1.42% wirelength reduction versus commercial EDA tools
primary_theme: Multi-bit flip-flop optimization through design-technology co-optimization
